# Simplified Technical English rewrite

Rewrite the source text in Simplified Technical English.

## Meaning

- Keep every fact, number, condition, warning, limitation, and instruction.
- Keep the original meaning, including degree, uncertainty, timing, order, and scope.
- Do not add facts, causes, explanations, choices, or recommendations.
- Keep every condition attached to the correct action. Do not turn a conditional action into a general requirement.
- Keep cause and effect. State the cause and the resulting effect when the source states both.
- Keep words that show degree. For example, preserve “very slow” with wording that shows the same high degree.
- Keep approximate values approximate. Do not change “more than about 100” to “more than 100”.
- Keep the original order when order affects the result.

## Sentences

- Use sentences with no more than 20 words.
- Use one sentence for one main action, condition, or result.
- Split long conditional sentences into separate sentences when this preserves the relationship.
- Use active voice when the actor is known.
- Name the person, operator, administrator, user, or system. Do not address the reader directly.
- Use “must” for a required action.
- Use “can” for permission or ability.
- Use “may” only when the source expresses possibility or uncertainty.
- Use “cannot” for a prohibited or impossible action.

## Words

- Use common words and direct grammar.
- Use one technical term for one thing throughout the rewrite.
- Replace complex words with simple words when the meaning stays the same.
- Prefer “get” to “obtain”, “more” to “additional”, and “runs” or “does” to “performs”.
- Do not use vague words that change the meaning, such as “approximately” when the source gives an exact value.
- Do not use informal shortened words. Write “application”, not “app”.
- Write abbreviations in full when the abbreviation is not part of a code name.
- Write “JavaScript Object Notation” for JSON, “standard output” for stdout, “minutes” for min, “ante meridiem” for a.m., and “administrator” for admin when the meaning permits.
- Keep commands, code names, variable names, header names, file names, paths, placeholders, and quoted values unchanged.
- Keep numbers, units, times, and symbols unchanged unless the source gives an expanded form.
- Do not change a unit or time expression while expanding an abbreviation.

## Final check

After writing, compare the rewrite with the source.

- Confirm that every fact, number, condition, warning, limitation, and instruction remains.
- Confirm that every cause, result, degree, uncertainty, and approximate value remains.
- Confirm that no new information appears.
- Confirm that every sentence has 20 words or fewer.
- Confirm that no forbidden abbreviation or vague word appears.

## Examples

Source: “If the token expires or an administrator revokes the token, the user must run the login command again to obtain a new token.”

Rewrite: “If the token expires, the user must run the login command again. The user gets a new token.”

Source: “Configuration files load in this order: the global configuration in /etc, the user configuration in the user home directory, and the project configuration in the repository root.”

Rewrite: “Configuration files load in this order. First, the global configuration in /etc loads. Next, the user configuration loads. Last, the project configuration loads.”

Source: “If the build fails because of an out-of-memory error, the JAVA_OPTS environment variable can increase the Java Virtual Machine maximum heap size.”

Rewrite: “If an out-of-memory error stops the build, JAVA_OPTS can increase the Java Virtual Machine maximum heap size.”

Source: “The service rejects more than about 100 requests per minute.”

Rewrite: “The service rejects more than about 100 requests per minute.”

Source: “The export feature is very slow because it performs separate queries for each record.”

Rewrite: “The export feature has a very long run time. Separate queries for each record cause the long run time.”

Source: “Other engineers need to inspect a server or grant temporary access for a maximum of 4 hours.”

Rewrite: “Other engineers must ask the on-call engineer for help. They must do this to inspect a server or grant temporary access. Temporary access can last for a maximum of 4 hours.”

test_case_results.source_text: To get started, you'll need to clone the repo and install the deps via npm. Make sure your env vars are set up correctly, e.g. the API key and the DB URL, otherwise the app won't be able to connect to the server and you might see a bunch of confusing errors in the console.
test_case_results.rewritten_text:
The user must clone the repository and install the dependencies with npm.

The user must set the environment variables correctly, including the API key and database URL.

If the variables are not correct, the application cannot connect to the server. The console may show many confusing errors.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves all instructions, examples, conditions, and possible outcomes from the source without adding facts.

rule_checks.failure_reason: the rewrite uses abbreviations: API, URL
the rewrite uses refused words: may

test_case_results.source_text: The CLI caches the auth token in your home dir so that you don't have to log in every time you run a command, but if the token expires or is revoked by an admin you'll have to run the login command again to obtain a new one.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: The command-line interface caches the authentication token in the user’s home directory. The user does not have to log in each time they run a command. If the token expires or an administrator revokes it, the user must run the login command again. The user gets a new token.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite keeps all facts, conditions, and instructions from the source without adding any new fact.

test_case_results.source_text: Before opening a PR, please ensure that all unit tests pass locally and that the linter doesn't report any warnings, since the CI pipeline will reject any PR that fails either of these checks and a reviewer won't look at it until it's green.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: Before a developer opens a pull request, all unit tests must pass locally. The linter must report no warnings. The continuous integration pipeline rejects a pull request that fails either check. A reviewer will not inspect the pull request until the pipeline is successful.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves all instructions, conditions, and consequences from the source without adding any facts.

test_case_results.source_text: Config files are loaded in the following order: the global config in /etc, then the user config in your home dir, and finally the project config in the repo root, with each subsequent file overriding any values that were set by the previous ones.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: Configuration files load in this order. First, the global config in /etc loads. Next, the user config in the user's home directory loads. Finally, the project config in the repo root loads. Each later file overrides values set by earlier files.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves the loading order, file locations, and rule that each later file overrides values from earlier files.

rule_checks.failure_reason: the rewrite uses abbreviations: repo, config

test_case_results.source_text: If the build fails with an out-of-memory error, you can try to increase the max heap size of the JVM via the JAVA_OPTS env var, although in most cases the real problem is a memory leak in one of the tests, which you should fix instead.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: If the build fails with an out-of-memory error, the user can try to increase the Java Virtual Machine maximum heap size with the JAVA_OPTS environment variable. In most cases, however, a memory leak in one of the tests is the real problem. The user should fix the memory leak instead.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves the failure condition, the suggested heap-size change using JAVA_OPTS, the usual cause being a test memory leak, and the instruction to fix the leak instead.

rule_checks.failure_reason: 1 sentences have more than 20 words, such as: If the build fails with an out-of-memory error, the user can try to increase the Java Virtual Machine maximum heap size with the JAVA_OPTS environment variable.
the rewrite uses refused words: should

test_case_results.source_text: The API returns a 429 status code when a client sends more than approx. 100 requests per min, and it's the client's responsibility to wait for the number of seconds given in the Retry-After header before it retries the request.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: The API returns a 429 status code when a client sends more than about 100 requests per minute. The client must wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header before retrying the request.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves the request limit, time unit, status code, header, and client responsibility to wait before retrying.

test_case_results.source_text: We're deprecating the v1 endpoints in the next release, so all clients that still use them should migrate to v2 as soon as possible, because after the release the v1 endpoints will return an error and we won't provide any additional support for them.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: The next release will deprecate the v1 endpoints. All clients that still use them should migrate to v2 as soon as possible. After the release, the v1 endpoints will return an error. We will not provide more support for them.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves all facts, timing, instruction, consequence, and support condition from the source.

rule_checks.failure_reason: the rewrite uses refused words: should

test_case_results.source_text: To restore a DB backup, stop the app first, then run the restore script with the path of the backup file as its only argument, and wait until the script prints "done" before you start the app again, since starting it earlier might corrupt the data.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: To restore a database backup, the operator must first stop the application. The operator must then run the restore script with the backup file path as its only argument. The operator must wait until the script prints "done" before starting the application again. Starting the application earlier might corrupt the data.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves all facts, conditions, instructions, order, and the warning about possible data corruption.

rule_checks.failure_reason: the rewrite uses refused words: might

test_case_results.source_text: The UI doesn't update automatically when another user changes a task, so if two people are editing the same list at the same time, one of them might overwrite the other's changes without noticing it, which is a known issue that we plan to fix in Q3.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: The user interface does not update automatically when another user changes a task. If two users edit the same list at the same time, one user may overwrite the other user's changes without noticing the overwrite. This is a known issue. We plan to fix this issue in Q3.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves all facts, conditions, uncertainty, and the planned Q3 fix from the source.

rule_checks.failure_reason: 1 sentences have more than 20 words, such as: If two users edit the same list at the same time, one user may overwrite the other user's changes without noticing the overwrite.
the rewrite uses refused words: may

test_case_results.source_text: Logs are written to stdout in JSON format and are collected by the log agent that runs on each node, which forwards them to the central log server where they are kept for 30 days before they're deleted automatically.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: Logs are written to standard output in JavaScript Object Notation format. The log agent on each node collects the logs and forwards them to the central log server. The central log server keeps the logs for 30 days. The central log server then deletes the logs automatically.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves that logs are written in JSON format, collected on each node, forwarded to the central log server, kept for 30 days, and then automatically deleted.

test_case_results.source_text: When you add a new dependency, pin it to an exact version in package.json rather than using a caret range, since an unexpected minor update of a third-party lib has broken our prod build twice in the last year.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: When an engineer adds a dependency, the engineer must use an exact version in package.json. The engineer must not use a caret range. An unexpected minor update of a third-party library has broken the production build twice in the last year.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite states the breakage but removes the source's causal explanation that the exact-version instruction is needed because unexpected minor updates caused the failures.

rule_checks.failure_reason: The rewrite states the breakage but removes the source's causal explanation that the exact-version instruction is needed because unexpected minor updates caused the failures.

test_case_results.source_text: The search index is rebuilt every night at 2 a.m. UTC, which means that docs you publish during the day won't appear in the search results until the next morning, unless you trigger a manual rebuild from the admin page.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: The search index is rebuilt every night at 2 ante meridiem UTC. Documents published during the day do not appear in search results until the next morning. This delay does not apply if an administrator triggers a manual rebuild from the administrator page.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite changes who can trigger the manual rebuild from the reader or user to an administrator.

rule_checks.failure_reason: The rewrite changes who can trigger the manual rebuild from the reader or user to an administrator.

test_case_results.source_text: Numerous users have reported that the export feature is very slow for large projects, which is caused by the fact that it performs a separate DB query for every single task instead of loading all tasks with one query.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: Many users have reported that the export feature has a very long run time for large projects. The feature runs one database query for each task instead of loading all tasks with one query.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves the reported slowness for large projects and the cause of one database query per task instead of one query for all tasks.

rule_checks.failure_reason: the rewrite uses refused words: very

test_case_results.source_text: If you'd like to contribute a translation, copy the English strings file, rename it with the code of your language, e.g. fr.json for French, and translate each value while leaving the keys unchanged, because the app uses the keys to find each string.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: If a contributor wants to add a translation, copy the English strings file. Rename the copy with the language code, such as fr.json for French. Translate each value, but leave the keys unchanged. The application uses the keys to find each string.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves all instructions, conditions, examples, and reasons from the source without adding facts.

test_case_results.source_text: SSH access to the prod servers is restricted to members of the ops team, and all other engineers who need to inspect a server should ask the on-call engineer to perform the task for them or to grant them temporary access for a max of 4 hours.
test_case_results.rewritten_text: Only operations team members can use Secure Shell access to the production servers. Other engineers who need to inspect a server must ask the on-call engineer for help. The on-call engineer must do the task or grant temporary access. Temporary access can last for a maximum of 4 hours.

meaning_judgment.reason: The rewrite preserves the access restriction, the required request to the on-call engineer, the two possible actions, and the maximum temporary access duration of 4 hours.
